title: Working Ethel Waters' club and meeting Louella
summary: He and Pete Johnson worked Waters' Chicago club; Louella, a flower girl, bought him ties.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So, I came to Chicago. Had one place I hadn't played. I'd been skippin' all aroun' Chicago. So we went...I started workin' in a place that Ethel Waters owned...in a nightclub. Pete Johnson and myself, we got a job at Ethel Waters's nightclub. So, the meantime, we was goin' to another club where T-Bone worked at, an' I met my first wife there. She was a flower girl...sold cigarettes and candy an' flowers an' dolls an' stuff. So I met her in the nightclub. So she lived at the Woodside Hotel. So, we were livin'--me and Pete Johnson was livin' in another hotel down the street 'bout four...five blocks, so she said this was a better hotel where she lived at.
There was a Woodside in Chicago?
There was a Woodside Hotel in Chicago?
No, no. It wasn't the Woodside. They called it the...ohhhh, what in the devil is the name of that place?
Well, maybe you'll think of it later, and we'll just put it in when you think of it.

So, we moved over to this new hotel where she lived at, so we wanted to buy some clothes---some ties and shirts and stuff. So we didn't know nothin' about Chicago. We never been there before. So Louelly...she live in the hotel...my wife that I married this lady later on...she said that she would go downtown for us and pick up some ties an' stuff. So I give her a coupla hundred dollars an' tol' her bring me back some shirts and some...coupla neckties...stuff, so she went downtown for me an' brought me back a who-o-o-o-ole lot of stuff. So I asked her, I say, "Where you...where do you...where you get the money to pay for all this stuff?" So she told me that she paid for it, that I could give it back to her. I say, "Well, how you know that I'll do that? How you know that I won't leave town? Just skip out and just let you...leave you holdin' the bag?" She said, "I don't think you'll do that. And anyway, I wanted to do it 'cause I wanted to see you look nice in the nightclub where you workin' at, and these are somethin' I like." So that brought on a little more talk. So I went on back to the club I workin' for Ethel Waters. So one night she came over to the club. She been in there 'bout an hour...maybe better. She was sittin' at the bar. I had never seen her with all her clothes on...dressed up...so I didn't know who she was. Had a veil over her face an' ever'thing. So I happened to go up to the bar, and I was jivin' with the bartender...
